Once routed through the correct (systemd-unit, --model gemma4:cloud) path, a full 50-chunk hand-run pass against the post-138 population completed in 16.677s wall-clock time per journalctl -- confirming that MAX_CHUNKS=50 is not, by itself, a throughput bottleneck for this task's measured backlog once the pass is invoked correctly. This directly informs 'THE CHUNK CAP' question in the dispatch: raising MAX_CHUNKS or prescribing a periodic wider backfill pass is not indicated by this reading alone.

The dispatch's own Description names two equivalent ways to hand-run a pass: 'sapience sync' in a terminal, and 'systemctl --user start sapience-sync.service'. They are not equivalent on this machine. The systemd unit's ExecStart passes '--model gemma4:cloud --backend ollama' explicitly (confirmed by reading /nix/store/vrlfwqq67bczbls4nv6h856mkn4sbcgw-sapience-sync); the bare 'sapience' wrapper's sync subcommand execs extract_local.py --sync --yes with no --model flag at all, so it falls back to extract_local.py's own per-backend default of 'llama3.1' (a local, not cloud-forwarded, model) rather than the home.nix-configured programs.sapience.model = "gemma4:cloud". Running bare 'sapience sync' by hand cold-started a local llama-server process pinned to 98-100% CPU on a single thread (-t 1) that had not completed even one of the queued chunks after 580 seconds, at which point the wrapping 'timeout 580' killed it with exit 124 and zero chunks/objects recorded (sapience coverage's own yield counter read '0 chunks in 0 runs' immediately after). Re-running the exact same backlog via 'systemctl --user start sapience-sync.service' immediately afterward completed all 50 available chunks in 16.677s wall-clock / 2.848s CPU time per journalctl's own unit-exit line, because that path's explicit --model flag forwards to Ollama's cloud endpoint instead of loading a 4.9GB local model from a cold cache.

Pass 1 (systemd-unit path, correct model) processed 50 chunks across 70 queued sources but staged zero new knowledge objects ('Staged 0 new knowledge objects locally (0 awaiting review)' per journalctl; sapience pending reads 0 immediately after). This is recorded as an observation to track across the remaining passes, not a conclusion: a single zero-yield run could reflect low-information early turns in the processed sources rather than an extraction defect, and the task's own step 3 (sapience review spot-check across the full series) is the designed place to resolve this.

The pass-1 systemd-unit run's apparent 16.677s success was a false positive: journalctl -u sapience-sync shows every one of the 50 attempted chunk-extraction calls to Ollama's cloud endpoint failed identically with 'extract error: HTTP Error 402: Payment Required', so the run's '0 objects' yield reflects total extraction failure, not low-information content. home.nix's own comment states gemma4:cloud is 'Free on Ollama's usage page, same as beam', but the live account this machine's OLLAMA_API_KEY authenticates as is being billed (and presumably not funded) for every call right now. This means the properly-configured extraction path (the one the systemd unit and home.nix's programs.sapience.model both point at) currently extracts nothing at all -- not a slow backlog-drain problem but a complete inability to produce findings via that path. The only path that was observed to actually attempt real inference (bare 'sapience sync', which silently falls back to the local, non-cloud 'llama3.1' default because extract_local.py's MODEL default is keyed off --backend not programs.sapience.model) was killed by this dispatch's own 580s guard before a single chunk finished, so whether it would eventually succeed, and at what per-chunk rate, once warm, is still unverified.

The task description's own framing of the question this task answers is now partly obsolete, and the plan had to reframe it rather than follow it literally. The description treats MAX_CHUNKS=50 drain rate as the binding constraint and names 'extraction spends real money or CPU per run' only as a caveat against backgroundSync. Post-migration the live numbers invert that: one 50-chunk pass staged 1208 knowledge objects against a 2000 objects/day cap (so ~60 percent of a day's cap in a single pass), took 29 minutes rather than seconds, left 1208 objects in an unreviewed queue, and is billed per call to the user's Anthropic key. The backlog it drains is small by comparison (78 'would ingest now' of 1153 on disk). The binding constraints are now the daily object cap, the review-queue depth, and per-pass cost -- not the chunk cap.

METHOD step 3 of this task's description instructs the implementer to 'read through sapience review output', but ~/.sapience/extract_local.py's --review path is interactive and share-capable: review_queue() prompts at line 1175 and review() at line 1920 prompts 'Press Enter to share ALL, numbers like 2,5 to DROP those'. An unattended agent running 'sapience review' against the current 1208-object queue could push the entire queue to the hosted vault or drop it. The plan therefore substitutes a read-only audit of ~/.sapience/pending_kos.jsonl (1208 JSON records carrying subject/predicate/object_value/ko_type/confidence/reasoning/open_thread/sid/project), which discharges the same intent without the share hazard, and states the substitution explicitly in the phase.

Premise re-validation at the start of this plan dispatch caught that the research report's central blocker is already resolved and its every figure stale, saving a wasted dispatch. reports/02_...md documents HTTP 402 Payment Required on all 50 gemma4:cloud calls and sets a blocking user_decision on Ollama billing; commit 2b713bf ('sapience: move extraction to the anthropic backend') resolved that by a route none of the four offered options named -- home.nix now sets backend=anthropic, model=claude-haiku-4-5, apiKeyFile=/run/secrets/anthropic_api_key, and the deployed unit /nix/store/qc34qy2m0g978zlqisblv4lghzajyf4p-sapience-sync passes --backend anthropic --model claude-haiku-4-5. A real pass then completed 2026-11-13 11:37:47-12:06:52 (29min 4.283s wall, 50 chunks, 1208 objects staged, zero extract errors). Planning from the report's figures unchecked would have produced a plan for a backend that no longer exists.

Pass 2 (sapience-sync.service, 2026-11-17T21:00:38Z-21:23:08Z, 22min 29.8s wall clock) recorded 34 non-zero extract error lines in the journal (3x 'read operation timed out', 30x DNS 'Name or service not known', 1x SSL handshake timeout), clustered in the final ~2 minutes of the run (13:16-13:23 PST), apparently a transient network/DNS outage rather than a billing/auth failure like the earlier ollama 402 series. Unlike that total-failure case, this run still staged 539 of its 50-chunk batch (539 objects, pending grew 1208->1747), so it is a partial failure. Per the plan's own risk mitigation, any pass with a non-zero extract-error count is excluded from the clean drain-rate computation in phase 7, so this Pass-2 datum must be flagged rather than averaged in.

sapience-sync.service is Type=oneshot and holds ActiveState=activating/SubState=start for its entire run (never transitions through ActiveState=active). A first polling attempt using 'systemctl --user is-active --quiet' (which only matches ActiveState==active) returned a false-positive DONE after ~2.5 minutes of a run that actually ran ~22.5 minutes. Corrected to poll ActiveState via 'systemctl --user show -p ActiveState --value' and loop while it reads 'activating' or 'active'. This is reusable for phases 3-5's identical pass-waiting step.
